paper.title: Incentive-aware Contextual Pricing with Non-parametric Market Noise

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated contextual second-price auctions with reserve against strategic buyers (strategic setting)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: seller chooses a contextual reserve price r_t in [0, v_max] for a second-price auction with N>=2 buyers
Buyer valuations v_{i,t} = <beta, x_t> + eps_{i,t}, beta unknown, eps i.i.d. from unknown non-parametric distribution F with bounded support and density bounded above (c_f) and below
Seller observes all submitted bids (not only the auction outcome), but bids may be corrupted b = v - a with |a| <= a_max
Buyers are strategic and maximize long-term discounted utility with discount factor eta in (0,1)
Contexts x_t i.i.d. from unknown distribution with positive definite covariance (min eigenvalue lambda_0), ||x||_inf <= x_max
The learner knows v_max (valuation upper bound)
settings.definition_quote: In each auction $t\in [T]$, an item is sold to $N$ buyers, where the item is characterized by a $d$-dimensional feature vector $x_t$ ... $v_{i, t} =\langle \beta, x_t\rangle + \epsilon_{i,t}$ ... each buyer $i\in [N]$ aims at maximizing his long-term discounted utility ... $b_{i,t} = v_{i,t} - a_{i,t}$ where $|a_{i,t}| \leq a_{\max}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated contextual second-price auctions with reserve, truthful buyers
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: contextual reserve price in second-price auction with N>=2 truthful buyers, all bids observed
Valuations linear in context plus non-parametric i.i.d. noise F with bounded support and bounded density
settings.definition_quote: in a hypothetical world where buyers are truthful (i.e. $v_{i,t} = b_{i,t}$ or equivalently the degree of corruption $a_{i,t} = 0$ for all $i \in [N]$, $t\in[T]$)

algorithms.name: NPAC-S (Non-Parametric Contextual Policy against Strategic Buyers)

symbols.c_f: supremum of the density of the market noise distribution F on its support
symbols.eta_disc: buyers' utility discount factor eta in (0,1)
symbols.N: number of buyers in the auction

conditions: T >= max{(8 x_max^2/lambda_0^2)^4, 9}, lambda_0 minimum eigenvalue of context covariance
N >= 2 buyers maximizing long-term discounted utility with discount eta in (0,1)
noise density bounded above by c_f and below by a positive constant on bounded support
valuations in [0, v_max]; bounded corruption |a_{i,t}| <= a_max
contexts i.i.d. with positive definite covariance, ||x||_inf <= x_max

source.label: thm:strat:Regret
source.quote: Suppose that the length of the horizon $T \geq \max\{ \big(\frac{8x_{\max}^2}{\lambda_0^2}\big)^4, 9 \}$ where $\lambda_0^2$ is the minimum eigenvalue of covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Then, in the strategic setting, the T-period regret of the NPAC-S policy is in the order of ${\mathcal{O}\Big(c_f \sqrt{dN^3 \log(T) }\cdot \log\left(\log(T)\right)\big( \sqrt{T} + \frac{\sqrt{N^3 \log(T)}T^{\frac{1}{4}}}{\log\left(1/\eta\right)} \big)\Big)} $

results.notes: Regret defined as sum of expected (REV*_t - rev_t(r_t)) against clairvoyant per-context optimal reserve (expected revenue, so pseudo-regret style). Paper says T unknown to seller, but phase lengths T^{1-2^{-l}} use T, so recorded horizon as known. Feedback mapped to full_information since all bids observed, though bids may be strategically corrupted.

symbols.c_f: supremum of the density of the market noise distribution F

conditions: noise density bounded above by c_f and below by a positive constant on bounded support

source.quote: in a hypothetical world where buyers are truthful ... our proposed NPAC-S policy achieves a regret of $\mathcal{O}(c_f \sqrt{dN^3T\log(T) }\cdot \log\log(T) )$ compared to the clairvoyant benchmark policy in Definition \ref{def:benchmark_policy}.

results.notes: Stated in text as a remark, proof omitted; presumably inherits the T condition of Theorem 1.
